DI registration center: AdminHandlers and Handlers struct fields are the sole compile-time link between TK handler implementations and the application. Dropping any field silently deregisters the corresponding TK surface (routes still reference the handler but get nil, causing runtime panics or silent 404s). The 8 anchors cover all TK-only struct fields across both structs.

Wire provider functions and ProviderSet entries that construct TK handlers with post-construction wiring (e.g. SetModelListFilter, SetAvailabilityService). Without these providers, Wire regeneration would fail to resolve TK handler dependencies — but if the providers are dropped AND the struct fields are dropped together (e.g. a clean upstream merge), the app compiles and silently loses the TK surfaces. These 9 anchors cover every TK-specific Wire provider.

TK compliance gate on admin page-list endpoint: setting-gated middleware that blocks admin page listing when compliance mode is enabled. This is a single-line insertion in an upstream-shaped file — trivially lost on merge, compiles cleanly without it, but silently disables the compliance guard on the admin pages route.

TK setting fields for canonical OAuth hardening toggles (ingress strict + haiku mimicry) and the cold-start diff helper call site. These are woven into the upstream-shaped GetSettings/UpdateSettings response/request structs and the settings diff function — dropping them compiles cleanly but silently removes the admin UI's ability to toggle canonical OAuth guards and loses cold-start setting change audit trail.

The generated server graph must inject one capability owner into both native gateway handlers. Losing either setter creates protocol-specific drift while the capability service and authenticated UI endpoint continue compiling.
Generated production DI evidence for the UniversalCapabilityService and both gateway projections. Source providers alone do not prove the real server graph retained the post-construction injection.
AdminHandlers must retain the supplier-source management owner. Removing this field together with its route wiring can compile cleanly while silently deleting the only supported operations surface.

Canonical supplier-source route owner: discover start + job poll, channel-scoped defaults from the family-rule SSOT, validate configured models, project via sync, and probe compatibility aliases mapped to the discover handlers. Activation/pause and legacy models-discover routes stay unregistered.

Generated production graph for the final supplier-source chain: one repository, account-domain commands, an account store with no group dependency, the real in-memory probe adapter, existing secret encryption, and the admin handler. Provider declarations alone do not prove the deployed server retained this isolated graph after Wire regeneration or an upstream merge.
